topics.topic: A19 timestamp responsibility for bindings and flows
questions: Are `bindings` and `flows` A19 consumers that obtain all their record timestamps from `clock`, or is another module supposed to supply those timestamps to them?
Are `bindings` and `flows` A19 consumers responsible for obtaining their record timestamps from `clock`, or must another module supply those timestamps to them?

quotes:
The table is the one mapping;
`30_trace.json` records the same:

### Knows

`models` (effect classes), `data_provider`, `canonical_values`, `clock`,
`store`, `functions` (contract versions), `bindings` (binding status and
declared classes).
judgement.why: The exhaustive mapping omits `bindings` and `flows` as A19 consumers even though both module definitions declare a dependency on A19's sole clock module.

topics.topic: Ownership mapping for A07 disclosure-class assignments
questions: Which modules own the A07 rules that assign disclosure classes to trial-case/trial-execution outputs and service outputs?
Are `functions` and `effects` consumers and partial owners of A07, or must those class assignments belong to one of the consumers named in the table?

quotes:
The table is the one mapping;
`30_trace.json` records the same:

The module that writes a
StoredValue M21 or a SpooledFile M22 sets its class, by one rule (A07 rule 3)
computed with `canonical_values.highest_disclosure_class`: `flows` for
constants (the class the composing agent declared, A07 rule 2), `runs` for
flow inputs (the port's class) and for function outputs, values and files
alike (the highest class received), `effects` for service outputs, values and
files alike (the binding's declared class), `functions` for trial cases and
trial outputs (a case input, authored or captured, the class its contract
input port declares; an expected output and a trial output, the highest class
of the case's inputs; M21).
judgement.why: The exhaustive A07 mapping excludes `functions` and `effects`, while the class-assignment passage explicitly gives both modules parts of A07 rule 3.

topics.topic: Ownership of A15 rule 6 for the repair view
questions: Who owns A15 rule 6: `surface`, `runs`, or another listed A15 module?
Does `surface` own A15 rule 6 and therefore belong among A15's consumers, or does another named A15 consumer own the repair-view rule?

quotes:
The table is the one mapping;
`30_trace.json` records the same:

`surface`, which may know every
module, assembles every read the State 0 inspect and read-a-trace actions
list, and the repair view of one slot (A15 rule 6, K-12), from the owning
modules' read capabilities and `store.page_records`.

A16: the one MCP entrance — request size, token comparison in constant time
against the installation's current list, the operation schemas and their
bounds, the actor table of A16 rule 3, handling one request at a time to its
end, run advancement included (A18 rule 3), paging parameters, the reads of
inspection, traces and the repair view of a slot (A15 rule 6), and responses that
carry no secret, path or stack trace; ending the process when a module returns
the stop of an unconfirmed cleanup, after that module has written its record
(above, "Unconfirmed cleanup").
judgement.why: The exhaustive A15 mapping omits `surface`, while the inspection and `surface` ownership passages explicitly assign A15 rule 6 to it.
